# Photo Print: Size & Layout

> iPhone and iPad app for printing photos at exact physical sizes. Official App Store listing: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6808903369

## Product facts
- App Store rating: 5.0 average from 8 ratings worldwide (checked 15 November 2026).
- iOS / iPadOS 17 or later. AirPrint, PDF, or 4 × 6 JPEG sheet export for a photo lab or store kiosk. Photo Print creates the file; it does not place print orders. Lab charges are separate.
- Photo sizes in inches, centimetres and millimetres. A4, US Letter and 4 × 6 paper.
- Photos that cannot fit are reported rather than shrunk.
- First completed output and three saved layouts included. Optional Pro (weekly or yearly subscription, or a one-time lifetime unlock) for unlimited outputs, unlimited layouts and saved page setups. Regional prices are shown in the app.
- Photos stay on the device. Purchases use Apple / RevenueCat; the other-apps section can query Apple's catalogue.
- ID and passport sizing and a head-size guide; no official compliance verification or acceptance guarantee.

- Free printer test-sheet PDFs are available on the website. The free in-app printer check is available now in Settings → Check your printer’s size.

## Free browser tools
- [Photo printing tools](https://usephotoprint.com/tools.html): index of the free tools below. They run in the browser, need no account and never upload photos.
- [Photos per page calculator](https://usephotoprint.com/photos-per-page-calculator.html): how many photos of a size fit on 4 × 6, 5 × 7, A4, US Letter, A5, A6 or Legal paper, with margins, gaps, paper direction and a to-scale preview. Uses Photo Print's own layout rules (checked against the app's code). Examples: six 2 × 2 in or eight 35 × 45 mm (landscape sheet) on borderless 4 × 6; twenty 2 × 2 in on US Letter with ¼ in margins.
- [Photo print quality checker](https://usephotoprint.com/photo-print-quality-checker.html): choose a photo (opened locally) or type its pixel size, pick a print size, see PPI after cropping, Photo Print's rating (Excellent ≥300, Good ≥200, Fair ≥150, Low below), what the crop removes and the largest size at 300 and 200 PPI.
- [Photo crop calculator](https://usephotoprint.com/photo-crop-calculator.html): what 4 × 6, 5 × 7, 8 × 10, 3.5 × 5, wallet, 11 × 14, 8.5 × 11, A4 and square prints cut off a photo or a 4:3, 3:2, 16:9, 1:1 or 19.5:9 shape. A 4:3 iPhone photo loses 11.1% to a 4 × 6 print; a 3:2 photo loses none.

## Printing guides and tools
- [How to print a photo at a specific size on iPhone](https://usephotoprint.com/print-photo-specific-size-iphone.html): The Photos app has no print-size field; set any width and height in inches, cm or mm, check A4/Letter fit (8 × 10 in fits Letter, not A4 with normal margins), choose Fill or Fit and print at 100%.
- [How to print locket photos from iPhone at the right size](https://usephotoprint.com/print-locket-photos-iphone.html): Measure a locket insert, make a custom-size rectangular photo, print at actual size and trim by hand.
- [AirPrint photo printing: missing printer, margins and paper](https://usephotoprint.com/airprint-photo-printing-troubleshooting.html)
- [Photo print resolution: pixels, PPI and cropping](https://usephotoprint.com/photo-print-resolution-ppi.html)
- [Photo Printed the Wrong Size? Causes and Fixes (iPhone, PDF, Printer) — Photo Print](https://usephotoprint.com/photo-printed-wrong-size.html)
- [iPhone Photo Printing Apps: Compare Four Workflows](https://usephotoprint.com/photo-printing-apps-iphone.html)
- [Photo Size Calculator: Pixels, Inches, cm and mm](https://usephotoprint.com/photo-size-calculator.html)
- [How to Print 1 × 1 Inch ID Photos from iPhone](https://usephotoprint.com/print-1x1-id-photos-iphone.html)
- [How to Print 2 × 2 Inch Photos from iPhone](https://usephotoprint.com/print-2x2-photos-iphone.html)
- [Print 35 × 45 mm photos from iPhone](https://usephotoprint.com/print-35x45-mm-photos-iphone.html)

- [Wallet Size Photo Dimensions & How to Print from iPhone](https://usephotoprint.com/print-wallet-photos-iphone.html)

The printer-test-sheet guide includes a local-only print-scale helper: measured ruler length / labelled length × 100. It diagnoses one measured length and does not certify printer accuracy or ID acceptance.

The photo-lab sheet is exactly 4 × 6 inches (101.6 × 152.4 mm); a service may label this 10 × 15 cm. The photo-lab guide explains how to check actual dimensions and avoid resizing to literal 100 × 150 mm.
